content.content: When invoked as `deccy draft <node>... [--edit <id>]` with one or more node ids, the deccy CLI shall open one draft for each node named, counting a node named twice as two, each in a workspace of its own, write each draft's record `open`, and report each draft's handle together with the workspace path that holds it.
content.rationale:
The sentence is the opening verb's whole answer, and each of its clauses is licensed by one prerequisite — szvotxpq for the surface, kwqnrzoz for the record, lpkssxpp for the workspace's place — none of which it amends. The trigger is the invocation surface (szvotxpq) and nothing else: the surface fixes the verb and its two argument positions, the node list and the optional edit flag, so the trigger is that invocation read as a condition rather than a second description of the verb; it is scoped to a call naming at least one node because the surface puts a call naming none on the refusal side, and a refusal is not an opening, so scoping by the trigger keeps the refusal where it belongs instead of promising an opening for an empty list. The verb is named and not paraphrased, so that no second spelling can claim the same response.

One draft for each node named, counting a node named twice as two, is the draft model's count (szvotxpq) read off the argument list: the list is the sequence of names the call gives, and because the model gives a draft exactly one node and allows a node several drafts, the count follows the namings rather than the distinct nodes and never folds a node named twice into one; the count is said out loud because a list of ids invites the reading that the drafts are per distinct node, which the model does not have. That clause is what the following one needs rather than a limit on size: the drafts are separate objects, so each can be placed apart from the others.

Each in a workspace of its own states possession and deliberately not place. Where a draft's working copy is created is settled by lpkssxpp, so this sentence names no root, no namespace and no derivation from any field, and the two cannot disagree about a directory; what it does say is one workspace per draft (szvotxpq, read from the draft model), which is what keeps two drafts of one call from meeting in one working copy.

Writing each draft's record `open` names the record and the state (kwqnrzoz), not the graph and not the store. The record's shape — the key it is held under, the references it carries, the file it lives in — is settled by kwqnrzoz, so this clause fixes no field, no filename and no location, and the state is named because a draft the verb has just opened has landed nothing and `open` is therefore the only state it can hold; naming `landed` here would require a landing this verb does not perform. The clause is per draft because the record is per draft: one record for three drafts would leave two of them without the thing that picks them out.

Reporting each draft's handle together with the workspace path is the smallest report that leaves every draft the call opened reachable. The node and the edit alone cannot pick a draft out, because a node may be held by several drafts at once, while the handle is the record's own key (kwqnrzoz) and the path is the location the record names (kwqnrzoz, placed by lpkssxpp), so the reported pair is the record's own fields read back rather than a second identity the CLI would have to keep. The clause fixes which pair is reported and not how it is printed: the line's exact text, its separator and its stream are not fixed here and answer to the CLI's output conventions, so naming content rather than format keeps this requirement from owning a rendering it was never given.

What the sentence leaves unsaid is as much a part of it as what it settles: the handle's format and minting, the jj name of a draft's workspace, how a node id is resolved to a node, what a call does when a named id names nothing, what a failed workspace creation or record write leaves behind, and any exit status. Each belongs to a commitment of its own and each can be settled without changing anything here. One requirement, one answer: for each node the call names, a draft with a workspace of its own and a record `open`, both reachable through the handle and the path it is reported with.
